notes: This release fixes what happens when a posting is RETRIED — after a failure, a crash, or a correction on screen — and how a correction is dated. The cheque you actually wrote is now the cheque that gets registered: retrying after changing the number used to register neither cheque (the spoiled number outstanding for ever, the one handed over in no register at all) or both (one payment showing two cheques). The app now stops and names both numbers. A retry from a different bank is caught, where before the app reused the first draft and credited one bank while the cheque was written on the other. An entry now lands in the accounting period its own date falls in: with last year reopened for an audit adjustment, twenty-three screens were stamping work with the wrong period and the ledger refused it. A correction now carries the same date as the reversal it replaces, so the expense and the credit that cancels it fall in the same month. And a check that cannot read the data now says so and stops, instead of treating the failure as permission to carry on — which could double fuel coupons on hand, file a second depreciation run, or skip an over-budget warning silently.
